Family
As a teenager my Dad (people knew him as Tony) moved from Carlsbad, New Mexico to Hayward in the 1950’s. He lived with his aunt on Chenault Way across the street from the Hayward Airport.
My parents married in the 1960's and they began their lifelong investment in Hayward by purchasing their first home on Gaither Way in the Schafer Park Neighborhood. My Dad worked hard his whole life. He worked in the Tire Department at Sears at Southland Mall and he was a Chabot College student. My Dad was a Police Officer for the City of Oakland for 18 years and he was so proud of his industrial steam cleaning business he built and operated for 10 years. When my Dad died he was an investigator for the State of California Health and Human Services Department. My parents were married for 32 years when my father died and I am sure he’s pleased that today he’s buried at Lone Tree Cemetery in the city he moved to over 50 years ago and loved so much.
My Mom’s story is similar to many Hayward families. From New Mexico too, my Mom moved to Hayward when she married my Dad. People know my mom as Lorina or Lori and she worked at United Can, a company that manufactured all of the cans for Hunts Cannery. She worked at BART for many years and today she's enjoying retirement from Alameda County. My Mom over the years has been incredibly active in Hayward and the Hayward Area. From the St. Bede Woman’s Club to President of the Hispanic Chamber of Commerce of Alameda County to Board Member of the Seventh Step Foundation. Both of my parents believe in the principle 'leadership through service' and today I have followed the path my parents paved for me many years ago.
I am a proud Hayward native. I was born at St. Rose Hospital and I grew up in South Hayward in the Schafer Park Neighborhood. I attended Eldridge Elementary School, St. Bede Catholic School, 3 R's Middle School in San Leandro, and I graduated from Hayward High School. I transferred from Chabot College to San Francisco State University where I earned a bachelor’s degree in La Raza Studies and a Master’s degree in Educational Administration and Public Policy Studies.
I am an educator and my career started over 30 years ago at San Francisco State University. Today, I teach Ethnic Studies and History at Chabot College and I occasionally lecturer in the Ethnic Studies Department at California State University, East Bay.
Since 2010, I have had the honor and privilege to represent Hayward neighborhoods and families on the Hayward City Council. As your Council Member, I have steered Hayward through an economic crisis, a housing crisis, and a global pandemic while simultaneously maintaining good and quality city services families and businesses expect. After two successful re-elections, in 2022 I was elected Mayor of Hayward. Today, I lead a strong council and I have the unique opportunity to lead Hayward into a stronger economy. My central focus over the years has been to listen to neighborhoods and then make local government responsive to neighbors and businesses. I am proud of my record always supporting public safety; making it easier for entrepreneurs and businesses to grow in Hayward; solving Hayward's housing and homelessness crisis; as well as making Hayward an Education City. I am especially proud of my record for unapologetically fighting for Hayward kids and making sure they grow up in a city with lots of opportunities.

# #voteforsalinas
## Endorse Mark
The Mark Salinas for Mayor of Hayward 2026 campaign is rooted in one core belief: our neighborhoods and families come first. Every priority we advance and every decision we make is guided by the voices of residents who care deeply about their blocks, their schools, and their future.
As Mayor, my responsibility is clear: to deliver the best services possible for our community. That means safe streets, clean neighborhoods, strong public safety, responsive city services, and real results that families can see and feel in their daily lives. I take that responsibility seriously, and I am committed to doing the work every single day.
This campaign is about continuing that work and doing it together.
Your endorsement matters. It reflects a shared commitment to strong neighborhoods, reliable city services, and a city government that shows up and delivers for families. With your support, we can keep moving Hayward forward and ensure every neighborhood receives the attention and investment it deserves.
I respectfully ask for your endorsement. And if you believe in this work, please share it with your family, friends, and neighbors. Together, we can build momentum, stay focused, and deliver for Hayward.
Thank you for your support and I humbly ask for your vote on November 3rd.
Goal: 186 endorsements

# #voteforsalinas
## We Endorse Mark!
It is truly humbling to receive the support of so many leaders, advocates, and community members from across Hayward. I am deeply grateful for the trust placed in me by elected officials, commissioners, neighborhood leaders, and community advocates who work every day to make our city the best possible place for all.
I’m especially appreciative of the support of my colleagues on the City Council. I do not take that trust for granted. It reflects our shared commitment to work together. We're focused, disciplined, and united under one mission: deliver for every neighborhood and every family.
Every endorsement represents trust, and I carry that responsibility with humility and gratitude. The support of respected leaders and community voices reinforces our commitment to serve all families.
This campaign reflects the diversity and spirit of Hayward. Neighbors, families, and leaders are coming together with a shared commitment to service and opportunity.
If you share this vision, I invite you to join us.
Thank you for your continued support and for believing in Hayward’s future.
